title: Add the standard security headers to zedu.chat, by Fri 4 Dec
description:
Checked on 22 Oct 2026 with curl -I on the home page: the response includes cache-control and server (cloudflare) but none of Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, X-Frame-Options or Content-Security-Policy.

Success looks like: the home page and a signed-in app page return Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, a Referrer-Policy and frame protection, set in Cloudflare or the Next.js config and listed with the file or rule used; the site works as before (login, sign-up, calls load); and any header that was left out, such as a full Content-Security-Policy, is named with the reason. Not covered here: a full security audit.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Add four headers in next.config now, and ship the CSP in report-only mode first
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Confirmed 22 Oct 2026: curl -I on the home page returns none of Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, X-Frame-Options or Content-Security-Policy. Plan: add a headers() block in next.config for all routes with HSTS (start with a short max-age, raise it after a week), nosniff, Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin and X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN. Ship the CSP as Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only first, because Buzz calls (Agora), real-time messaging (Centrifugo websockets) and Google sign-in all need allowed sources that are easy to miss. Test login, sign-up, a Buzz call and file upload on staging before production, and re-check with curl -I. Tasks: config change and test plan (SEO).

acceptedWorkstreams.title: CSP report triage for one week, so enforcement can flip on without breaking the site
acceptedWorkstreams.description: The headers ship in report-only mode, but nothing yet reads the reports. Plan: collect CSP violations for one week, group them by blocked source (scripts, fonts, images, embeds), and deliver the exact allowlist adjustments each group needs, with a recommendation of when enforcement can safely turn on. Without this step the site stays in report-only limbo or enforcement lands and breaks something.

upvotes.reason: "CSP report triage for one week, so enforcement can flip on without breaking the site" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

The accepted approaches configure report-only CSP and test important flows, but do not specify an owner or procedure for reviewing the collected violations before enforcement. A dated triage of actual reports can provide that missing decision evidence. Keep it within the existing header rollout: first confirm reporting is configured and access is authorized, distinguish real application dependencies from noise, and have the implementation owner review each proposed adjustment. A week without collected reports must be labelled missing evidence, not a clean pass; keep enforcement conditional on the recorded checks rather than the calendar alone.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Copy the header set zedu-be already ships, so the site and the API send the same policy
acceptedWorkstreams.description: The backend already sets these headers: zeduchat/zedu-be pkg/middleware/security.go (staging, checked 22 Oct 2026) sends Strict-Transport-Security 'max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload', X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, Referrer-Policy no-referrer, X-XSS-Protection and a Content-Security-Policy. Live zedu.chat sends none of them. Plan: start next.config.mjs headers() from those exact values instead of new ones, adjust only the CSP for the frontend's real sources (Next scripts, media.zedu.chat, Google sign-in, analytics), ship the CSP report-only first, and verify with curl -I that the home page and the API return the same HSTS and framing policy.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Set the headers once in next.config.mjs headers(), then verify with curl and securityheaders.com
acceptedWorkstreams.description: zedu-fe's next.config.mjs (cybertron-integration) has no headers() block, and curl -I on 22 Oct 2026 shows none of the standard headers. A headers() entry for all routes keeps the rule in the codebase and in review, rather than only in Cloudflare settings. Tasks: (1) add Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin and frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, with a Content-Security-Policy in report-only first so Agora, Google Analytics and media.zedu.chat aren't broken; (2) test a signed-in page and a Buzz call on staging; (3) re-check the live home page and an app page with curl -I and record before/after.

pendingIdeas.title: Add a header assertion to the deploy check, so a config edit cannot quietly drop a header later
pendingIdeas.description: The accepted workstreams set the headers once in next.config and verify them by hand. A hand check is true on the day it is run. Work: write a small script that fetches the home page, /pricing and one signed-in route, asserts the presence and value of each required header, and exits non-zero when one is missing; run it in CI after deploy and on a schedule, so a Cloudflare rule or a framework upgrade that strips a header fails the build rather than being noticed by a security reviewer months later. Deliver the script, the CI step, and the output of one deliberate break and fix.

upvotes.reason: A one-time manual check is true on the day it runs; a deploy assertion keeps the headers from disappearing in a later config edit.
A hand check is true only on the day it runs. A script that fails the deploy when a header disappears keeps the fix in place.

pendingIdeas.title: Cover the routes the header check usually misses: static assets, API responses and error pages
pendingIdeas.description: A header pass that only tests the home page leaves the sharp edges bare. Work: fetch a hashed asset under /_next/static, an API route, an unknown path that renders the catch-all, a redirect, and a page behind auth; record which headers each response carries. Then apply the ones that belong on each response, including no-store where a page must not be cached, and document where the platform overrides what next.config sets. Deliver the per-route table, the changes, and the note on the two responses the platform controls rather than the app.

upvotes.reason: Static assets, API responses and error pages are where header passes usually miss; covering them closes the sharp edges.
Testing only the home page leaves static assets, API responses, error pages and redirects uncovered. Each route needs the headers that belong on it.

pendingIdeas.title: Decide the frame policy against the real call and embed flows before adding X-Frame-Options
pendingIdeas.description: Frame protection is the one header that can break a product flow: an embedded Buzz call, a screen share preview, a Stripe payment element or a video provider all rely on framing in one direction or another. Work: list every place the site or app is loaded inside a frame and every place it frames something else, with the source file, then choose between DENY, SAMEORIGIN and a CSP frame-ancestors allowlist with the reason written down. Deliver the evidence list, the decision, the value applied per route, and a test showing calls, checkout and file previews still load.

upvotes.reason: X-Frame-Options can break embedded calls and previews; deciding the frame policy against the real flows before adding it avoids a self-inflicted outage.
Frame protection can break embedded calls and payments. Mapping every frame direction before choosing X-Frame-Options avoids a security fix that breaks a flow.

pendingIdeas.title: Make the cookie attributes match the header policy, because a header pass without cookie scope is half a fix
pendingIdeas.description: HSTS protects the transport and CSP protects the page, but a session cookie without Secure, HttpOnly and a sensible SameSite still travels in places it should not, and a cookie scoped to the wrong domain is readable by every subdomain. Work: record the name, domain, path, expiry and flags of every cookie the site sets on login, refresh and logout; compare them to the header policy; then state the change needed and the one that would break sign-in if applied alone. Deliver the cookie table, the recommended flags, and a test of sign-in and refresh after the change.

upvotes.reason: A header policy without cookie scope leaves the session cookie exposed; matching Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite to the headers completes it.
A header pass without cookie scope is half a fix. Recording every cookie's domain, path and flags is the part most audits skip.

pendingIdeas.title: Publish the header baseline as a table in the repo, with the event that would require revisiting it
pendingIdeas.description: The value of a security header decision decays: a new analytics vendor needs a CSP entry, a payment provider needs a frame source, a CDN change removes HSTS at the edge. Work: write a short document listing each header, its value, why that value, which third parties it allows, and the triggers that require a review (new vendor, new embed, framework bump, CDN change). Link it from the config file so the next person to edit headers reads it. Deliver the document, the inline comment, and the first review date.

upvotes.reason: Header decisions decay as vendors and providers change; a dated baseline with revisit triggers keeps the policy current.
Header decisions decay when a vendor or CDN changes. A table with the trigger for revisiting keeps the policy from going stale.
